title: Terraform storage bootstrap: KMS defaults, cross-region archival, and automated health checks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: provide a single, well-documented Terraform module (modules/storage-core) used by Redwood Private installs that: 1) creates EBS/EFS/S3 resources with secure-by-default encryption settings and sane lifecycle defaults, 2) supports optional customer-managed KMS keys while falling back to Redwoods-managed KMS when appropriate, 3) automates cross-region archival/copy for S3 and EBS snapshots, and 4) integrates health checks and scheduled drift detection runs.

Scope and constraints:
- Module surfaces constructs for EBS (volumes & snapshots), EFS (filesystems + backups), and S3 buckets (data + artifacts). Not responsible for higher-level app provisioning.
- Must work in Private (VPC) mode with cross-account roles for Enterprise tenants.
- Minimal run-time IAM footprint: recommend separate IAM role for snapshot management and cross-region copy.

Key behaviors and defaults we decided on (Design decisions):
- KMS selection: variable kms_key_id optional string. If empty, module uses an account-scoped Redwood-managed CMK alias (alias/redwood/private-storage) and documents how customers can supply their own. Rationale: lowers friction for trial installs while keeping a clear path to customer-managed keys for regulated customers.
- Encryption enforcement: all created EBS/EFS/S3 resources enable server-side encryption by default (EBS: encrypted=true, EFS: kms_key_id, S3: server_side_encryption_configuration).
- Immutable S3 retention (Object Lock) is optional boolean enable_object_lock default=false. We avoid enabling by default due to data lifecycle/restore complexity; customers with strict retention can opt-in and will be required to provide a retention configuration and approved KMS key.
- Snapshot cadence and cross-region copy: module can optionally create DLM lifecycle policies for EBS snapshots and S3 replication configurations for cross-region archival. Default: daily snapshot, retain 14 days, cross-region copy disabled by default to avoid cost surprises.
- Safe remediation: module will not perform destructive in-place mass-encryption. If it detects unencrypted resources in preflight checks, it will: (a) fail the plan (config drift blocker) and (b) provide an automated remediation playbook (PR template + infra-runbook) that creates encrypted copies and schedules a migration. Trade-off: avoids silent destructive changes during infra runs but requires operator step for migrations.

Health checks and automation:
- Terraform plan guard: we add a pre-commit/CI check in the infra repo that executes a policy scan (regula / sentinel style) to prevent proposals that omit encryption or set retention below minimum.
- Nightly drift detection: a scheduled Terraform Cloud run (or Atlantis job) runs `terraform plan` against Private installs, sending diffs to an internal Slack channel (#infra-drift) and creating incidents for critical drifts (unencrypted volumes/keys changed).
- Resource-level monitoring: CloudWatch metrics and Config Rules to detect unencrypted EBS/S3/EFS and to verify snapshot schedules are present. Alerts create PagerDuty incidents with runbook links.
- Automated reconciliation: for low-risk issues (missing snapshot policy), an operator-configured Lambda can create the missing policy. For high-risk issues (unencrypted volume), we do not auto-remediate; instead we open a migration ticket and optionally run a migration job after manual approval.

API/Inputs (high level):
- variables: name_prefix, kms_key_id, enable_cross_region_copy, cross_region_targets (list), enable_object_lock, snapshot_retention_days, snapshot_schedule_cron
- outputs: primary_bucket_arn, default_kms_key_arn, snapshot_policy_id

Trade-offs considered:
- Auto-encrypting existing resources vs manual migration: auto-encrypting in-place is technically complex and could cause data loss; opted for operator-assisted migration path to minimize risk.
- Cross-region copy enabled-by-default vs opt-in: chosen opt-in to avoid large egress costs unexpectedly for customers.
- Using Redwood-managed KMS by default vs forcing customer KMS: default speed for onboarding balanced with clear docs for customer KMS.

Implementation notes / developer checklist:
- [x] Core variables, outputs, and documentation skeleton.
- [x] S3 bucket module with SSE and optional Object Lock wiring.
- [x] EBS volume construct + sample DLM policy module.
- [ ] DLM lifecycle module tests and acceptance in staging. (blocked by test account quotas)
- [ ] CI guard implementation (policy rules) and integration with Terraform Cloud runs.
- [ ] Add migration helper scripts (terraform import + snapshot copy) and PR templates.

Testing plan:
- Unit: terratest for module (create/destroy) with mocks for KMS.
- Integration: end-to-end run in a dedicated staging account including cross-region copy to us-west-2.
- Chaos: simulate missing KMS key and plan to verify guard fails and runbook triggers.

Rollout strategy:
1) Merge module behind feature flag and enable only on sandbox installs.
2) Run module in audit mode for 2 weeks (create plan-only runs) and collect diffs.
3) Enable auto-policy creation for low-risk policies (snapshot scheduling) after verification.
4) Offer migration service/workflow for existing customer unencrypted volumes.

Operational runbooks and links: See attachments for detailed runbooks and example PR templates.

Metrics to watch post-rollout:
- Percentage of Private installs using customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed (target: 25% by Q3).
- Number of drifts detected per week and mean time to remediation.
- Snapshot success rate and failed cross-region copies.
